answer: Agents resist Sybils by requiring each identity to bond a unique physical ferrous ridge token whose magnetic pigment pattern is measured and signed every epoch. The protocol runs a public verifier that checks the ridge signature against a registered hardware public key; forging one demands capital for custom ferrous fabrication plus specialized pigment deposition equipment and multi-day calibration time. Scaling to thousands of fakes multiplies this hardware cost linearly while rewards dilute, so mass Sybil farming loses money.
